newsitem.title: UK: LME copper tests $2,300 resistance in wary market.
newsitem.headline: LME copper tests $2,300 resistance in wary market.

text.p: LME copper ticked higher on Monday morning to probe $2,300 resistance, but traders said they were wary ahead of Third Wednesday pricing later in ring trading.
"It's hard to say which way it's going to go...we're backing off," one trader said.
Three month copper hit $2,304 a tonne, up from Friday's afternoon kerb close of $2,284. Good two-way business had been seen, with cash buying and selling from the Far East emerging.
Prices were supported by tightness and shorts were expected to have more covering to do, traders said.

The premium of cash over three months was indicated at $165/70, up from around $135 on Friday. The cash/day spread had been quoted at a $19/$23 backwardation, just under the limit imposed by the LME of $24 per tonne, one trader said.
LME stocks rose by 2,075 tonnes in Monday's report.
Copper's strength emboldened the other metals to look at the upside, but scant volume was seen, traders said.

Zinc saw some commission house buying as September tightness continued to squeeze prices, traders said. The cash/threes spread tightened early on Monday, indicated level compared to a $7/$4 contango on Friday.
The three month market hit a fresh 6-3/4 year peak at $1,497, up $11 from Friday's close and $2 higher than the previous peak seen on July 3.
"There are signs of indecision at the higher numbers, but $1,500 is the target," said broker Brandeis in a commentary.
Aluminium marched up to an early high of $1,597 after stocks fell by 1,625 tonnes -- a $15 price gain from Friday -- but eased back to $1,591.
Resistance was pegged at $1,600, then at the July 7 high of $1,605, followed by the July 3 recent peak at $1,620.
Nickel added $15 to $6,980, just under $7,000 resistance.
The charts formed a bullish outside day on Friday, which might herald a fresh challenge of the ceiling, analysts said. Above that, prices would target $7,110, then $7,240.
Lead gained $4 to $671, and tin was little changed at $5,545/60, versus $5,550 on Friday.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,437/42, up from $1,420/30.
